newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks end higher, bond market provides lift.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks end higher, bond market provides lift.

text.p: Wall Street stocks finished with solid gains on Tuesday, boosted by a strong performance in the bond market that sent interest rates to their lowest levels in nearly eight months.

The Dow industrials rose 53 points to close unofficially at 8175, the second consecutive record high for the blue chip average. Interest rate sensitive stocks paced the rally, with financial and cyclical issues posting strong advances.
Financial markets got a double dose of good news to start the session.

The news included word of a bipartisan deal to balance the U.S. budget and a U.S. Labor Department report that showed labor costs rose 0.8 percent in the second quarter, in line with economists' forecasts.
A subsequent rally in the bond market sent the yield on the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury down to 6.38 percent, its lowest since December 3.

"If you're looking for a story in stocks today, bonds are the story," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "The budget deal helped and the data showed the economic backdrop remains the same, sugar sweet."

Rate sensitive stocks paced the rally, with American Express Co gaining 3-9/16 to 82-7/16, the biggest rise among Dow components. J.P. Morgan & Co Inc rose 3-1/2 to 114-1/4 and Caterpillar Inc climbed 2-3/16 to 59-3/4.

"Money just seems to be pouring into the rate sensitive financials and cyclicals," said Guy Truicko, portfolio manager at Unity Management. "Right now, investors seem to be delighted with the economic environment."
Investors still face a series of critical economic reports over the rest of the week, culminating with monthly payrolls, wage and manufacturing data on Friday.

Analysts said the data, coupled with the fact that the corporate earnings reporting season is drawing to its conclusion, would likely shift the stock market's focus back towards bonds and interest rates over the next few weeks.

Among individual issues, Cyrix Corp rose 1-7/8 to 24-15/16 after announcing late yesterday that it had agreed to be acquired by National Semiconductor Corp. Shares in National Semiconductor fell two to 31.
Citicorp rose 6-7/16 to 130-9/16 after Merrill Lynch raised its near-term rating on the shares to buy from accumulate.
PLC Systems Inc tumbled 12-3/16 to 13-5/16 after a U.S. Food and Drug Administration panel recommended that the FDA reject the company's laser system for treating certain heart conditions.
Galileo Technology Ltd GALTF.O jumped 10-1/4 to 27-1/4 in the semiconductor company's first session of trading following its initial public offering.
The S&P 500 index rose 5.84 points to 942.29, a record.
The Nasdaq Composite gained 8.79 points to 1572.32.
